name: La Table du Castellet
address: Hôtel & Spa du Castellet, 3001 Route des Hauts du Camp, 83330 Le Castellet, Var, France
tier: THE BERTHS · THE SUMMIT — THREE STARS AND TWO
recognition: Three MICHELIN stars at once in March 2024 under Fabien Ferré, then 35 and the youngest three-star chef in France; held in the 2026 Guide France (16 March 2026). Gault&Millau 2026: 17/20.
what_to_order: Encornet à la provençale|Marine tasting menu|Plant tasting menu|Symbiosis menu|Barley, gavotte, kumquat and rye miso

reservation: Book ahead; reached by car
notes: Encornet à la provençale: squid cooked slow and flat, laid over chickpeas and finished with a poultry jus perfumed with fresh marjoram — one of Ferré's signature plates.
verdict: A three-star built on subtraction, not spectacle: fish or vegetable taken one at a time, each carried by a single full-bodied sauce. Judge it by the encornet à la provençale — flat-cooked squid under a marjoram-scented jus. If that plate doesn't justify the restraint, nothing on the menu will.
caveat: Not a village table: a dining room inside a five-star resort beside the Circuit Paul Ricard, reached by car, at three-star prices, under a young identity reopened in 2023. Expect precision and calm rather than Provençal rusticity. The hotel shuts for the winter from early December (2026 listing open to 1 December). Coordinates are approximate to the resort.

verdict: Two Michelin stars (won 2020, held in the 2026 Guide) for a Provençal kitchen that runs on olive oil, garden vegetables and the sea instead of butter — order the rouget poached in seawater and the cooking argues its own case. Falsifiable: it drops from two stars, or the plates arrive rich and heavy rather than featherweight.
caveat: The gastronomic table of a five-star domain: terrace only, seasonal (the resort reopened 1 May 2026; the 2026 end date was not found, and in 2025 La Voile closed on 12 October), priced around EUR 195–350 a head before wine. The stars date to 2020; 2026 confirms retention, not promotion. Philippe Starck's name belongs to La Réserve à la Plage on Pampelonne, not to this restaurant, whose buildings are Jean-Michel Wilmotte's.

name: Colette — Hôtel Sezz
address: Hôtel Sezz Saint-Tropez, 151 route des Salins, 83990 Saint-Tropez, Var
tier: ONE STAR BY THE SEA

notes: The house frames two tasting menus. The namesake gesture is the "Originel" — 100% plant-based, vegetables carrying the whole score rather than a garnish; the "Substantiel" alternative is built on the chef's signature dishes (oyster, squid risotto). Plant- and sea-leaning throughout. (These are the house- and tourism-listed signatures, not a single fixed dish.)
verdict: The one Saint-Tropez grande table where a courgette or a grilled oyster is asked to carry the plate rather than a slab of caviar. Falsifiable test: if the star is pulled, the menu turns meat-heavy, or the room stops running dinner-only, this verdict is wrong. As of the 2026 MICHELIN Guide France it holds one star, Colinet is still in the pass, and the "Originel" menu is genuinely 100% plant-based. Come for restraint and Provençal produce; skip it if you want a red-meat-and-oligarch-wine-list night.
caveat: Dinner only and seasonal: the 2026 season ran 1 May to 3 October and the room is dark now. Five- or seven-course menus at EUR 148–196. Menu names differ by source (the old record gives 'Originel' and 'Substantiel'; the 2026 tourism listing gives 'Substances' and 'Cuisiner les sens'), so check on booking. It sits out on route des Salins, east of the village, not in the old port.

name: Récif — Hôtel Les Roches Rouges
address: 90 boulevard de la 36ème Division du Texas, 83530 Saint-Raphaël (Boulouris)
tier: ONE STAR BY THE SEA

reservation: Booking required
notes: A vegetable-and-sea register the Michelin Guide now credits to Baule's kitchen: mackerel worked from head to tail, oysters from nearby Tamaris, squid cannelloni (Guide Michelin). Three tasting menus — from a fully plant-based "Tout végétal" through "Hommage à la Méditerranée" to the eight-course "Balade Gourmande" — roughly €150–€210.
verdict: Falsifiable: it has held one Michelin star every year since 2019 (Guide Michelin) — and, unusually for a kitchen that changed hands, the star carried over. José Bailly won it; Alexandre Baule took the stove in May 2025, and the current Michelin listing already describes his cooking, star intact. What changed is not the rating but the register — the strict no-meat identity is gone.
caveat: José Bailly's strict no-meat identity is gone: Alexandre Baule (from 14 May 2025) puts local meat beside the fish and vegetables and splits his year with Megève, so Récif is a spring-summer table only. In 2025 it served dinner Wednesday to Sunday; 2026 service days were not found. The hotel's 2026 season ended 10 October.

name: Shanael
address: 10 rue Molière, 83000 Toulon (place de l'Opéra, Vieux Toulon)
tier: ONE STAR BY THE SEA
recognition: One Michelin star, Guide Michelin France 2026 — announced 16 March 2026, four months after opening; plant-forward cooking backed by short-supply, seasonal sourcing.

notes: Artichauts juste saisis — boudin noir, pomme, jus végétal. The artichoke as manifesto: the vegetable carries the plate and the black pudding is kept to a whisper, the clearest read on what Denon means by "vegetables first."
verdict: Toulon's only Michelin-starred table — and its first in a generation. Denon opened opposite the opera in December 2025 and took the star four months later (Guide Michelin 2026, announced 16 March 2026) — vegetables leading, meat kept in support, sourcing as spine. Not the city's first star ever: Toulon had gone without one since La Chamade (chef Francis Bonneau) closed in 2001. Falsifiable: it is the sole starred restaurant in the city of Toulon, and the star came within a single season of opening.
caveat: Not a casual drop-in. A small room of roughly thirty to thirty-six seats (sources differ), so book well ahead. Dinner tasting menus run about €95–165 (weekday lunch from around €49) — a special-occasion table, not a value pick. Prices come from trade press, not the Michelin listing, and moved during 2026, so confirm when reserving.

name: Chez Bruno
address: 2350 route des Arcs, Campagne Mariette, 83510 Lorgues, Var, France
tier: THE HINTERLAND HOUSES — THE TRUFFLE, THE GARDEN, THE ABBEY
recognition: One MICHELIN star shown on the guide's current page for Bruno, Lorgues; no 2026-dated confirmation found
what_to_order: Potato baked in its skin under truffle|Black truffle (Melanosporum) menu|Uncinatum truffle menu|Vegetarian truffle menu
reservation: Book ahead; phone 04 94 85 93 93 per a 2015 article (not rechecked)
notes: "Le plat d'anthologie de la Maison Bruno" — a whole potato baked in its skin and buried under truffle (truffle cream and freshly grated tuber), the dish the house was built on. It appears on every menu.
verdict: A single-obsession pilgrimage: truffle threads every course of the fixed seasonal menu, amuse-bouche to dessert. Falsifiable claim — there is no non-truffle tasting path here (even the vegetarian menu is truffle-built); if you don't love the tuber, this is the wrong temple, and no clever à la carte will save you.
caveat: Not cheap and not for the truffle-indifferent. Truffle menus run roughly €98 to €218 before wine (children's menu €25). The black Melanosporum that made the house famous is a winter tuber — come off-season and it gives way to milder varieties (autumn Uncinatum or the white Albidum), a different and lesser thing. It sits in open country off the route des Arcs, not in Lorgues town; hours narrow to Tuesday–Sunday from mid-September to mid-June, so book ahead and check the calendar before you drive out.
hot_this_month: The black-truffle winter season starts with the Aups market in late November; here truffle runs through every course of the seasonal menu (checked 17 Oct 2026).

name: Le Faventia — Terre Blanche

If the star ever reads as resort-hotel decoration rather than earned, that lamb is where you'll catch the lie — or fail to.

Ducasse-group pricing, a ten-room inn deep in the countryside, a menu tied to the garden and the season, and a winter closure whose length differs by source.

name: Club 55
address: 43 Boulevard Patch, Plage de Pampelonne, 83350 Ramatuelle, Var (Côte d'Azur), France
tier: ON THE SAND — PAMPELONNE AND THE ISLANDS
recognition: The first restaurant on Pampelonne, begun as the canteen for the crew of Roger Vadim's 'Et Dieu créa la femme' (1956), Brigitte Bardot among the cast. No MICHELIN star.
what_to_order: Panier de crudités|Whole grilled sea bass|Strawberry tart|Provence rosé
reservation: Reserve ahead, essential in July–August
notes: Le panier de crudités — a whole basket of raw garden vegetables with hard-boiled eggs and a mayonnaise dip, drawn from the family's own farm (Ferme des Bouis, Ramatuelle).
verdict: Come for the myth, not the Michelin — there is no star here and never has been. The kitchen does one thing well: unfussy Provençal built on its own farm — the raw-vegetable basket, a whole grilled sea bass, a strawberry tart. Judge it as gastronomy and you leave disappointed and lighter of wallet; judge it as the first restaurant on Pampelonne, still run by the family that fed Bardot's crew in 1955, and it is the one table on this coast worth the trip for the place alone.
caveat: Ruinously priced and unapologetic about it — a whole fish, a rosé and two crudité baskets vanish into three figures fast, and sunbeds/parking are billed apart; it trades on scene as much as cooking. Seasonal: the 2026 season runs 27 March–1 November (shut in winter), and it heaves in July–August — reserve well ahead and expect no walk-in miracle. Lat/lng is approximate to the beach frontage.
hot_this_month: Last weeks of the season: listed open daily 10:00–17:00 until Sunday 1 November 2026; phone before going (checked 17 Oct 2026).

Falsifiable: seasonal, roughly mid-April to end-September, closed Mondays; mostly daytime, with dinner on Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday evenings in July-August.

name: Hôtel La Ponche

tier: THE OLD HOUSES — DATED

recognition: Listed in the MICHELIN Guide France 2026 without a star (modern cuisine, €€€); one Gault&Millau toque 2025 per the Saint-Tropez tourism listing.

price_range: Lunch menu about EUR 60, dinner menu about EUR 120, plat du jour EUR 48 (tourism listing, seen Oct 2026)

notes: The house-billed warm chocolate mousse with Fior di Latte ice cream; on the savoury side, the rock-fish soup (soupe de poisson de roche) and the grilled catch of the day off the terrace — all three named on the restaurant's own menu.
verdict: In the 2026 MICHELIN Guide it is listed with no star: book it expecting a rosette and you will be let down. What you are actually buying is the most storied address in Saint-Tropez's old fishermen's quarter and a terrace hung over the gulf, with Simon Pinault's market-Mediterranean cooking in the kitchen since concept chef Thomas Danigo moved on in 2025.
caveat: Not a bargain and not year-round. Saint-Tropez five-star prices: menus are reported around €60 at lunch and €120 at dinner, with a plat du jour near €48 (Saint-Tropez tourism listings; the house's own PDF menus omit prices, so treat these as indicative, not fixed). Dinner is served Tuesday to Saturday only (roughly 7–10:30pm); the gulf-side terrace is really a warm-season pleasure; and with just 21 rooms plus a handful of apartments the table fills — reserve well ahead.

price_range: Menus EUR 40-70, the EUR 40 menu at lunch only (tourism listing, seen Oct 2026)

The foie gras is a paid supplement (reported around €20), not a sliver of garnish. Falsifiable claim: if the terrines don't come to your table in tubs to help yourself, this isn't the place its regulars have eaten at for sixty years.
caveat: No cards: cash or French cheque. Probably shut for the winter since 11 October 2026; one listing ran the season to 21 October, so call before driving. One user-edited guide claims a 2024 founding and a single EUR 70 menu; the registry and tourism office contradict the founding date.
